The constitutional hierarchy

Authority descends.
Responsibility does not.

  1. 01

    The Crown

    Embodies the reigning source of authority.

  2. 02

    The Royal House

    Claims permanent ownership of engagement.

  3. 03

    The Great Houses

    Compete to produce, distribute, measure, and certify importance.

  4. 04

    Ministries and Institutes

    Convert prevailing conduct into policy, research, and administrative doctrine.

  5. 05

    The Peerage

    Awards territorial titles for dubious distinction.

  6. 06

    The Orders

    Grant cross-House honors for conspicuous achievement.

  7. 07

    The Subjects

    Follow, create, refresh, and occasionally attempt to log off.

Court precedence under Prompt I

The Six Great Houses

The Houses are constitutionally equal. Their precedence changes with each reign and whenever the dashboard needs to tell a better story.

01

Produces the content.

House of Prompt

AI generation, synthetic expertise, and automated creativity

The less one understands, the more confidently one produces.

Office of Synthetic Understanding

Pete Sine Intellegendo · Ask without understanding.

02

Keeps it moving.

House of Scroll

Attention, compulsion, and infinite feeds

Nothing is important, but everything must be seen.

Royal Institute of Digital Inquiry

Semper Deorsum · Forever downward.

03

Declares it important.

House of Influence

Status, visibility, personal brands, and public importance

Everyone is an influencer, leaving no one available to be influenced.

Chancery of Public Importance

Notus Quia Notus · Known for being known.

04

Proves it worked.

House of Signal

Analytics, dashboards, attribution, and evidence

Every decision is data-driven; the data is adjusted to support the decision.

Ministry of Measurable Outcomes

Quod Mensuratur Verum Est · What is measured is true.

05

Sends it to everyone else.

House of Spam

Scale, distribution, repetition, and unsolicited reach

If nobody responded, the audience was insufficiently large.

Ministry of Universal Correspondence

Ad Omnes Aeque · To all subjects equally.

06

Precedence pending.

House of Buffer

Delay, loading, postponement, and technical excuses

Everything is imminent; nothing is presently available.

Commission for Imminent Availability

Tandem, Fortasse · Eventually, perhaps.

The sovereign field

One standard.
Six jurisdictions.

The central check records legitimacy by verified appearance. The six charges identify the portfolios through which attention is produced, retained, declared important, measured, distributed, and indefinitely delayed.

The doctrine of convenient evidence

All decisions shall be data-driven.

All data shall be interpreted in accordance with the decision.

The peerage

A title describes the distinction.
A House explains the damage.

Institutions provide respectable justification. Orders recognize conspicuous achievement across House boundaries.

  1. 01

    Duke or Duchess

    Platform-scale compulsions and major cultural pathologies

    Duke of Doomscrolling · House of Scroll
  2. 02

    Marquess or Marchioness

    Unstable boundaries between online and offline, truth and opinion, or human and synthetic

    Marquess of Context Collapse · House of Signal
  3. 03

    Count or Countess

    Metrics, followers, views, impressions, and anything misleadingly counted

    Countess of Selective Analytics · House of Signal
  4. 04

    Viscount or Viscountess

    Secondary statistics and derivative status

    Viscount of Verified Reach · House of Influence
  5. 05

    Baron or Baroness

    Everyday digital indignities and minor technical failures

    Baron of Buffering · House of Buffer
